illusion_checker_shadow — GENERATIVE illusion op

• Data kinds: none → rgb (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.illusion_checker_shadow(size: 'int' = 46, n: 'int' = 8, light: 'float' = 0.62, dark: 'float' = 0.31) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import illusion; illusion.illusion_checker_shadow(size: 'int' = 46, n: 'int' = 8, light: 'float' = 0.62, dark: 'float' = 0.31) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsgenerative.get("illusion_checker_shadow"))

Usage

Checker shadow. The 2 marked squares have exactly the same pixel value.

Taking the shadow factor as dark / light makes a light square in the shadow and a dark square outside it numerically identical. ★This figure is drawn with aa=0 (no anti-aliasing) -- because blended edge colours would make the claim "exactly equal" the one that lies.

Invariant: the 2 squares in CHECKER_PATCHES -- the dark square outside the shadow (2,3) and the light square inside the shadow (5,5) -- have exactly matching pixel values (difference exactly 0).

★We got this wrong once. The pair must be "dark square × no shadow" and "light square × shadow"; picking 2 squares of the same shade naturally does not match (a measured difference of 0.31 appeared). The picture "looks right" anyway, so you cannot notice until you check with numbers -- the very same type of accident this family is meant to guard against.
